perf(storage): decouple Tx cleanup from writes and batch flushes (#346)

* perf(storage): wake Tx backlog admissions on progress

Park pressured admissions on worker-local notifications instead of request
polling and awaiting a complete cleaner round. Last-lease release and each
Tx block retirement wake waiters to recheck the existing global predicate.
Coalesce cleaner work into one background driver, preserve pressure retries
and error delivery, and join queued as well as running work during shutdown.

Add 11 deterministic runtime tests for progress races, threshold rechecks,
worker stop, shutdown, retryable maintenance and fatal maintenance errors.
Update the transaction and storage architecture for the changed flow.

Validation:
- Debug build, lavik_tx_backlog_admission and lavik_multikey_e2e pass.
- Release build and pre-commit pass.
- Local diagnostic build, 100 preloaded 1 MiB keys, 80 connections, three
  interleaved 20-second runs per version: median QPS 337.35 -> 351.52,
  average latency 236.725 -> 228.059 ms, p99 790.527 -> 684.031 ms,
  p99.9 942.079 -> 950.271 ms. The notification change does not remove
  sustained admission pressure; its threshold and lease lifetime are unchanged.

* perf(storage): pipeline writes independently of Tx cleanup

Remove the fixed sealed-Tx admission gate and synchronous grouped-write cleanup. Drive coalesced cleaning from sealed blocks and lease completion, retrying independently of foreground waiters, and release completed queue receipts without retaining their writer leases for the remaining batch.

Preserve allocator and commit-queue capacity limits, cleaner failure handling, and shutdown joins. Cover active-lease independence, autonomous cleanup progress, low-capacity recovery, and crash windows.

* perf(storage): batch ready flush data and avoid unchanged Tx rescans

Treat the configured 128 KiB size as a dirty-byte trigger and submit already available snapshots in writes up to 1 MiB. Continue threshold-sized tails accumulated during in-flight flushes while preserving sealed stream ordering and the data/header durability protocol.

Remember successful Tx promotion scans until accounting, dependencies or inverse publication invalidate them, while continuing destination fences and retirement checks. Cover flush triggers, batching, crash recovery and scan invalidation with deterministic tests.

* fix(storage): back off failed cleaner rounds and stabilize recovery tests

* fix(storage): await active transaction reclamation before reporting full

Simplify command dispatch and fix GCC coroutine test compilation (#352)

perf: batch collection RESP replies and inline point operands (#351)

* perf: batch collection replies and inline point operands

Collection replies append each bulk element separately even when the complete
result is already available. Size and encode bulk elements in one buffer
growth, projecting the existing packed results directly without temporary
view arrays. Preserve nullable Hash slots and RESP2/RESP3 container semantics.

Format sorted-set scores in caller-owned stack buffers and reserve scored
replies once. Inline the common single Hash/List operand while retaining
normal growth for batches. Cover nullable/binary replies, score spellings,
and Set aggregation source replacement and recovery.

* perf(redis): inline single ZSET command operands

SortedSetOperation already borrows spans, but ZADD/ZINCRBY/GEOADD and
member lookup/removal handlers allocate descriptor vectors for one member.
Inline one descriptor in each command-local owner while preserving batch
reservation, request order and existing input admission. Construct spans
after filling their owner and retain the owner across the awaited call.

Validate point and batched inputs, GEO replies, compact operations, recovery
and grouped writes suspended across preparation with four existing E2E cases.

* perf(redis): reduce Stream operand and reply allocations

Keep single Stream ID selections inline in delete, acknowledgement and group
access descriptors and in callback-local delete/claim lists. Move access
owners into the by-value storage calls so batches and consumer names are not
copied again across coroutine boundaries.

Reserve the complete XADD field/value count before copying request strings,
and encode materialized entry fields with the bulk reply batch writer.
Retain existing input admission, decoded entry layout and paged reply flow.

* fix(redis): avoid over-reserving scored range replies

The scored-range prepass reserves the maximum formatted score width for every
member, requesting substantially more space than short scores need. Let the
reply grow with the actual encoded values and remove the extra accessor pass.
Keep stack-based score formatting, plain bulk batching and the flattened-count
overflow guard, and update the surrounding sizing comments.
